methodological_rigor.justification: Multi-omics bioinformatics (TCGA, TIMER, CPTAC, HPA, Kaplan-Meier plotter) combined with IHC validation on 38 paired BRCA/normal tissue samples and QuPath-assisted digital pathology. Strengths include multi-platform concordance (mRNA, protein, IHC), use of both manual H-scores and automated QuPath with Bland-Altman agreement analysis, and multivariable Cox adjustment for age and comorbidities. Weaknesses: IHC cohort small (n=38, single center, retrospective), no functional wet-lab experiments (siRNA/CRISPR knockdown, rescue, or in vivo), mechanism inferred from GSEA and co-expression rather than demonstrated, and immune/PD-L1 correlations rely on bulk RNA-seq deconvolution. Statistical methods are appropriate for the data types with explicit BH correction and appropriate non-parametric tests.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Oxford 4: retrospective bioinformatic and IHC case series. Clinical relevance is plausible: identifies G3BP1 as a candidate prognostic/diagnostic biomarker associated with DFS (HR 2.51, 95% CI 1.07-5.90 after adjustment), lymph node involvement, and potential link to PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway and PD-L1. Diagnostic accuracy is moderate (AUC 0.777) and 5-year DFS AUC 0.730, suggesting potential complementary utility but not standalone clinical use. No prospective validation, no therapy-response data, no functional demonstration.

reporting_quality.justification: As a biomarker/prognostic study, REMARK is the relevant standard. The paper reports sample source (single hospital, Jan 2013-Oct 2014, n=38), inclusion/exclusion criteria, IHC scoring system and cut-points, multivariable Cox adjustment variables, and clinical endpoints (OS/DFS/DMFS/PPS). Gaps relative to REMARK include limited description of patient selection flow, no pre-specified analysis plan, and some endpoint definitions not fully detailed. Public databases (TCGA/TIMER/CPTAC/HPA/KM plotter) are used with URLs, supporting partial reproducibility; in-house IHC data not shared.

novelty_literature.justification: Authors claim to be among the first to systematically link G3BP1 to BRCA progression using multi-omics approaches. However, prior work (cited refs 25, 26) has already reported G3BP1 upregulation in breast cancer and functional effects on proliferation and metastasis (Liu et al. 2022, Ge et al. 2023 in endometrial cancer, Zhan et al. 2024 in NPC). The present study is a meaningful extension adding systematic prognostic analysis with multiple survival endpoints and subtype stratification, plus IHC+QuPath validation, but not a field-defining contribution. Novelty leniency guarded.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-structured with clear separation of database/bioinformatic analyses, mechanistic GSEA, and clinical IHC validation. Statistical details (thresholds, correlation coefficients, p-values, HRs with 95% CIs) are reported consistently. Figures and supplementary material are referenced systematically. Minor issues include occasional wordy passages in the Discussion and some redundancy between results and discussion. Overall readability is good.

key_strengths: Multi-omics concordance across TCGA mRNA, CPTAC proteomics, HPA IHC, and in-house IHC (n=38) supports robust G3BP1 upregulation finding
Digital pathology validation with QuPath agreement analysis (Spearman rho >0.89, minimal bias) adds methodological rigor to IHC quantification
Multiple survival endpoints (OS, DFS, DMFS, PPS) with subtype stratification (luminal A/B, HER2+, basal/TNBC)
Multivariate Cox adjustment yields significant independent prognostic value (HR 2.51, 95% CI 1.07-5.90)
key_concerns: No functional wet-lab validation (no knockdown/overexpression rescue, no in vivo) for the proposed G3BP1-PI3K/AKT/mTOR or PD-L1 mechanisms
IHC validation cohort limited to n=38 from a single center, retrospective
Mechanism claims (PI3K/AKT/mTOR activation, immune evasion, PD-L1 regulation) rely on correlative bioinformatics only
Contradictory-sounding immune-infiltration results between CIBERSORT (negative with CD8+, positive with M2) and TIMER (positive with all six cell types) are not reconciled
Novelty incremental given prior G3BP1 reports in breast and other cancers
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed multi-omics biomarker study with a small but carefully quantified IHC cohort, but lacking functional validation and reconciliation of some immune analyses; best fit is a mid-tier specialty oncology journal after major revisions adding mechanistic experiments.
